title: Research Scientist in Scientific AI and Geotechnical Engineering
description: EinleitungstextThe Chair of Geotechnical Engineering at ETH Zurich, part of the Institute for Geotechnical Engineering (IGT), focuses its teaching and research on foundation engineering, soil mechanics and natural hazards. Our objective is to combine theoretical knowledge with experiments and numerical simulations to develop new methods for understanding and predicting the behaviour of soils, foundations and infrastructure. We are opening a position in our research group at ETH Zurich, focusing on developing and integrating modern Artificial Intelligence (AI) methods into geotechnical engineering research, while maintaining a strong connection to the underlying physics and mechanics. We do not aim to develop a new AI model or replace physics-based engineering with purely data-driven AI. Instead, we want to use AI to transform the way research itself is performed—from numerical model generation and experimental data acquisition to analysis, visualization and communication.For this purpose, we are looking for a Research Scientist in Scientific AI and Geotechnical Engineering, who will work across the research group, collaborating with PhD students, postdoctoral researchers and senior scientists.The role combines scientific research, computational engineering, research automation, data science and the development of reusable AI-enabled tools. A central objective is to identify new opportunities where AI can enable research that would otherwise be difficult or impossible, and to develop capabilities that can be used across the entire group.Aufgaben-/StellenbeschreibungThe job will interconnect several different areas of our activity:Scientific AI and physics-informed modellingDevelop and apply AI and machine-learning approaches to challenging problems in geotechnical engineering and computational mechanics, with particular emphasis on approaches that combine data with physical knowledge, rather than relying exclusively on black-box, data-driven models.Explore topics including physics-informed and physics-guided machine learning, hybrid physics–ML constitutive modelling, surrogate and reduced-order models, inverse problems and parameter identification, uncertainty quantification, and AI-assisted scientific discovery.Apply these methods to problems involving soil behaviour, soil–structure interaction, liquefaction, natural hazards, foundations and infrastructure resilience.AI-enabled numerical modellingDevelop tools for automating and accelerating numerical modelling workflows, including finite element (FE) and potentially discrete element (DEM) and material point method (MPM) simulations.Automate tasks, such as model generation, geometry and mesh creation, assignment of materials and boundary conditions, parameter studies, high-performance computing (HPC) execution, model verification, extraction of results and standardised post-processing.Create robust and reusable tools that enable researchers throughout the group to build and analyse numerical models more efficiently while retaining appropriate engineering control and verification.Automation of experimental researchDevelop AI-enabled methods for the acquisition, processing and interpretation of experimental data from laboratory and centrifuge testing.Automate sensor-data processing, synchronization of different measurement systems, computer-vision analysis of experiments, extraction of deformation and failure mechanisms from images and videos, identification of experimental parameters, and integration of experimental and numerical results.Geotechnical data intelligenceDevelop methods to exploit the growing volume of geotechnical data available within the group and through external repositories.Organize and extract information from historical laboratory and centrifuge experiments and numerical analyses, and exploit large external datasets and research repositories such as DesignSafe and databases containing geotechnical and geological properties.Contribute to the longer-term development of structured, physics-aware geotechnical datasets to support parameter inference, model calibration, uncertainty quantification, identification of model deficiencies and the development of new physics-informed AI approaches.Scientific visualisation and communicationDevelop automated approaches for transforming research results into high-quality visualisations, animations and videos.Develop tools that support scientific publications and presentations while facilitating effective communication of research through websites, teaching materials, professional audiences and social-media platforms.Group-wide AI capabilityHelp establish AI as a broadly accessible research capability within the group.Identify opportunities for AI across ongoing research activities, develop common tools and workflows, provide internal training and documentation, and work directly with researchers to enable them to use modern AI and computational methods effectively and independently.Ihr ProfilWe are looking for an intellectually curious scientist / engineer who combines strong computational skills with an interest in physical systems and engineering research. A background in geotechnical engineering is not mandatory but can represent an advantage.PhD in computational mechanics, computational engineering, scientific machine learning, applied mathematics, computer science, civil or mechanical engineering, or a closely related discipline.Excellent programming skills.Strong background in numerical methods, such as FEM, FD, DEM or MPM.Demonstrated experience with machine learning, modern AI methods and AI-assisted software development.Experience with scientific data engineering, databases and the processing of large or heterogeneous datasets.Experience with HPC, parallel computing and/or GPU computing.Experience with automated simulation workflows and APIs.Experience with scientific visualisation and the automated generation of figures, animations or videos.Experience with computer vision and image/video analysis is particularly valuable.Candidates from other fields than geotechnical engineering with strong expertise in computational mechanics and Scientific AI are strongly encouraged to apply. The successful candidate will work closely with experienced geotechnical researchers who will provide the necessary domain expertise.Beyond specific technical qualifications, we are particularly interested in candidates who can bridge disciplines. The successful candidate should be able to understand an engineering or scientific problem, identify where AI or computational methods can provide genuine added value, develop a rigorous solution, and transform that solution into a reusable capability for other researchers.We therefore value scientific creativity, strong software-development practices, independence, collaborative ability and an enthusiasm for learning new areas.The position is particularly suited to someone who is excited by the opportunity to help shape a new research direction at the intersection of Artificial Intelligence, mechanics, experimentation and geotechnical engineering.Wir bietenThe opportunity to help shape a new research direction at the intersection of Artificial Intelligence, computational mechanics, experimentation and geotechnical engineering.Considerable freedom to identify research opportunities and contribute to the development of new methods as AI technologies and Scientific AI continue to evolve.The opportunity to work across scientific research, computational engineering, numerical simulations, experimental research and data science.Close collaboration with PhD students, postdoctoral researchers and senior scientists in an interdisciplinary research environment.The opportunity to develop reusable AI-enabled tools and workflows that strengthen research capabilities across the group.Neugierig? Applications via email or postal services will not be considered.We would like to point out that the pre-selection is carried out by the responsible recruiters and not by artificial intelligence.

description: The Portfolio Manager is allocated a defined amount of Master Fund trading capital and is individually accountable for the profit and loss generated on it. The role holder owns the complete investment process, from research and idea generation through portfolio construction, execution, risk management and performance attribution. The specific markets and style vary by individual; the expectations below apply to every Portfolio Manager in the Master Fund. It is a principal risk-taking position, not an analytical, advisory or support function: the Portfolio Manager makes the final investment decisions and bears direct responsibility for their outcome.Investment ManagementGenerate profits for the clients of the Brevan Howard Master Fund by trading the allocated capital on their behalf, within the pre-agreed trading mandate.Originate, research and develop macro investment ideas, building each thesis on fundamental, quantitative and technical analysis, with particular attention to central bank policy, growth and inflation dynamics and their transmission into global rates, FX, inflation, volatility and equity index markets.Construct a portfolio sized to conviction, liquidity and correlation, selecting the instruments and structures (cash securities, futures, swaps, options and other OTC derivatives) that give the most asymmetric expression of each view.Deploy capital through directional and relative value expressions as the market regime warrants, including balance-sheet-intensive trades where the opportunity justifies it. Flexibility of style and the ability to scale risk into a strong theme are expected of a Master Fund Portfolio Manager.Regularly reassess that the portfolio reflects the intended market view, and restructure or exit positions when a thesis is invalidated.Take hands-on responsibility for execution, counterparty relationships and liquidity sourcing, and ensure that any execution delegated to a trade analyst or execution trader is correctly implemented.Risk ManagementOperate at all times within the risk framework agreed with the Chief Investment Officer and Risk Management: capital allocation, VaR and stress limits, leverage and balance-sheet limits, concentration and liquidity constraints, and the fund’s drawdown limits.Manage live portfolio risk daily and intraday, for the role holder’s own book and for any allocation run by team members, actively managing drawdowns and demonstrating strict discipline in loss management.Liaise with the risk management team who deliver risk reports, articulating positions, rationale and sensitivities clearly and responding to challenge.Liaise with Treasury to ensure positions are properly funded and that collateral is placed effectively.Improve and scale risk-taking over time as the investment process is proven, in agreement with the Chief Investment Officer and Risk Management.Performance, Monitoring and ReportingMonitor, attribute and explain daily, monthly and annual P&L and risk, and articulate performance drivers clearly to the Chief Investment Officer, Risk Management and senior management.Deliver a return commensurate with the capital allocated, at a quality of returns (information ratio, drawdown profile, consistency across market regimes) consistent with the Master Fund’s expectations.Prepare periodic performance reports on a timely basis, monitor adherence to exchange and counterparty limits, ensure that all trading activity is appropriately allocated and accounted for, and maintain accurate records of the investment rationale for positions and decisions.Contribution to the Fund and the FirmContribute to the Master Fund’s investment dialogue, sharing views, data and expertise with the Chief Investment Officer, other Portfolio Managers and senior management in a collaborative manner.Where leading a team, take full responsibility for the hiring, development, output and conduct of analysts, traders and sub-portfolio managers, and maintain an ongoing commitment to their development.Present periodically to the investment management committee and, where required, support the Client Partnership Group with current and prospective investors.Governance, Compliance and ConductOperate at all times within the firm’s compliance policies, applicable regulatory requirements (including market abuse, conflicts of interest, best execution and personal account dealing rules) and the firm’s Code of Conduct; hold any regulatory certification the role requires in the relevant jurisdiction (for example the FCA Certification Regime in the UK); and act with integrity at all times. WORK EXPERIENCE/BACKGROUND:EssentialA minimum of 7–10 years’ experience in a principal risk-taking capacity, as a trader at a sell-side institution and/or as a Portfolio Manager, Sub-Portfolio Manager or Pod Portfolio Manager at a hedge fund or asset manager, trading global macro markets.A minimum of 3 years’ attributable, verifiable track record of managing risk capital, evidenced through audited or employer-confirmed P&L and risk reports, with the candidate’s own contribution clearly separable from that of any wider team.P&L of a scale that justifies a substantial allocation of institutional capital, together with evidence of having run a large book and of the ability to scale risk as capital grows.A high quality of returns, assessed through information ratio, maximum drawdown and recovery, hit rate and consistency across market regimes, with limited reliance on a small number of outsized trades. Returns generated through excessive leverage, concentration or tail-risk selling are not regarded as evidence of skill.Experience of running directional macro risk through periods of market stress and drawdown within a formal institutional risk framework, and of operating comfortably at the scale and volatility of a flagship global macro fund.A clearly articulated, proven and repeatable investment process that can be explained from first principles: the source of edge, how ideas are generated, how positions are sized and risk-managed, and how the process has adapted to changing market conditions.A strategy and return stream that would be diversifying within a global macro portfolio. DesirableExperience as a lead Portfolio Manager at a global macro hedge fund with a multi-asset mandate spanning developed and emerging markets.Experience of managing balance-sheet-intensive strategies and large gross exposures, including funding, repo and collateral management.Experience of building and leading a team of analysts, traders or sub-portfolio managers.Experience of expressing macro views across more than one asset class, for example rates and FX together with inflation, volatility, equity indices, credit or commodities.A postgraduate qualification (Master’s, PhD or MBA) and/or a relevant professional designation such as the CFA or FRM. TECHNICAL/BUSINESS SKILLS & KNOWLEDGE:EssentialExpert understanding of the pricing, mechanics, risk characteristics and regulatory treatment of global rates, FX, inflation and volatility instruments: government bonds, interest rate and cross-currency swaps, futures, options and swaptions, other OTC derivatives and financing instruments.A sophisticated understanding of global macroeconomics, monetary and fiscal policy, central bank reaction functions and their transmission into financial markets.Fluency in portfolio risk measures (VaR, expected shortfall, stress and scenario analysis, DV01, Greeks, factor exposures, liquidity and correlation risk) and in interpreting and challenging risk system output.Strong quantitative skills, including statistics, time-series analysis and derivatives pricing; technical data analysis skills, with Python or a comparable language and Bloomberg proficiency expected.Detailed knowledge of market microstructure, liquidity dynamics, execution venues and transaction cost management in the relevant markets.Working knowledge of the trade lifecycle, operational controls, counterparty and collateral arrangements, and the regulatory environment governing trading in the relevant jurisdictions.The ability to articulate complex investment views, risks and performance clearly and concisely to the Chief Investment Officer, Risk Management and peers, verbally and in writing.Judgement under uncertainty, intellectual honesty, discipline under pressure and resilience through drawdowns; self-motivated and accountable, and able to operate in a collaborative organisation with unimpeachable integrity.A strong undergraduate degree from a respected academic institution in a rigorous discipline such as economics, finance, mathematics, statistics, physics, engineering or computer science.DesirableExperience of building proprietary models, datasets and analytical tools, or of running a systematic overlay to a discretionary process.Established relationships with sell-side counterparties, brokers and liquidity providers

B. TOGAF)* Mehrjährige Erfahrung als ICT\-, Lösungs\- oder Enterprise\-Architekt/\-in, vorzugsweise mit Erfahrung in öffentlichen Organisationen oder IT\-Service\-Providern* Fundierte Kenntnisse in Enterprise Architecture sowie in der Gestaltung und Dokumentation von Daten\-, Applikations\-, Technologie\-, Security\- und Netzwerkarchitekturen* Erfahrung mit Architektur\-Governance, Technologieportfolios und Roadmaps sowie mit agilen Methoden wie Scrum und SAFe* Ausgeprägte analytische und kommunikative Fähigkeiten gepaart mit Problemlösungskompetenz, Beratungs\- und Verhandlungsgeschick sowie einer selbstständigen und kundenorientierten Arbeitsweise; Erfahrung mit modernen Technologien wie Microservices, Container\-Management und DevOps von Vorteil* Gute aktive Kenntnisse zweier Amtssprachen  **Auf den Punkt gebracht**Du bist ICT\-Architekt/\-in aus Leidenschaft? Du möchtest dein Wissen, deine Erfahrung und deine Hands\-on\-Mentalität im BIT einbringen? Als ICT\-Architekt/\-in hast du die einmalige Gelegenheit, komplexe und spezialisierte IKT\-Architekturen aus der bisherigen IT\-Provider\-Welt in neue Geschäftsfelder zu navigieren und substanziell mitzugestalten.  **Das bieten wir***  **Arbeiten für die Schweiz** Wir setzen uns für das Erfolgsmodell Schweiz ein und arbeiten zum Wohl der Bevölkerung.*  **Gelebte Vielfalt** Dank Chancengleichheit entfalten wir unsere Kompetenzen und bringen unterschiedliche Perspektiven ein.*  **Gesund am Arbeitsplatz** Wir unterstützen und beraten unsere Mitarbeitenden im Bereich der physischen und psychischen Gesundheit.  **Wieviel (B)IT steckt in dir?**Wir \- das Bundesamt für Informatik und Telekommunikation (BIT) \- sind das zukunftsorientierte und agile Amt. Bei uns entwickeln neugierige Köpfe, ambitionierte Macher/\-innen und innovative Vorausdenker/\-innen vielfältige digitalen Lösungen für die Schweiz. Wir unterstützen und fördern mobiles sowie ortsunabhängiges Arbeiten. So können unsere Teamplayer/\-innen ihre Arbeit wo möglich flexibel und individuell gestalten \- für die Vereinbarkeit von Familie und Beruf. Ausserdem pflegen wir im BIT eine offene Du\-Kultur und fördern dich und deine Zukunft mit einem breiten Aus\- und Weiterbildungsangebot.  **Zusätzliche Informationen**Bewirb dich bitte über unser Bewerbungsmanagementsystem.
